data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism asserted—heterogeneity avoiding monoculture and capping infection rates below 100%—does not establish that decentralized failures are causally independent rather than merely appearing uncorrelated. The biological-style mutation shield analogy is offered as mechanism but no evidence-generating test is proposed to distinguish true independence from latent shared causes. The countercondition (hyper-standardization) identifies a risk but does not supply the distinguishing evidence the problem explicitly demands. The mechanism also conflates exploit-propagation resistance with correlated-failure independence: heterogeneous configurations may all share a hidden dependency (e.g., a common upstream library or certificate authority) that produces correlated failures invisible until triggered, which the mutation-shield framing cannot detect or rule out.
